issues: Whether a non-renewal clause can be defeated by dishonest conduct in the exercise of contractual discretion
Whether the duty of honest performance under Bhasin v Hrynew was breached by active misrepresentation about renewal intentions
Whether damages are available for reliance losses caused by a party's misleading conduct during the term of a contract that allowed non-renewal
What remedies are available where a party fails to exercise a contractual right (non-renewal) honestly
Whether the misleading statements constitute negligent or fraudulent misrepresentation independent of the contractual non-renewal right
How damages would be measured (expectation vs reliance) if a breach of the duty of honest performance is found
key_facts: Contract contained a clause permitting non-renewal by either party
During the final year, the other party actively misled the client about its intentions regarding renewal
The misleading conduct caused the client not to seek alternative arrangements
causes_of_action: Breach of the duty of honest performance (Bhasin v Hrynew)
Breach of good faith in contractual performance
Breach of contract (bad faith exercise of non-renewal right)
needs_clarification: Which province or jurisdiction governs the distribution agreement (e.g., where the parties operate/contract was performed), since this affects which court's law and precedents apply?
